status_summary: The companies remain in conservatorship in the latest sources reviewed: Fannie Mae's own SEC filing of 2026-07-29 (second quarter 2026) still reports it in conservatorship and mentions no exit or offering, FHFA's conservatorship page says they continue to operate under it, and FHFA's news release listing through 2026-09-30 shows no release on an exit, an offering or capital. The administration has discussed a public offering since May 2025, and on 2025-11-07 FHFA Director Bill Pulte said the companies would stay in conservatorship while the government explored selling up to 5 percent of their shares. In January 2026 the President directed purchases of $200 billion of mortgage-backed securities, which Pulte said the companies would make and which a lawyer quoted by trade press said would delay an offering (Fannie Mae's first-quarter 2026 filing confirms FHFA raised its mortgage-backed securities investment limit in January 2026 but does not mention the $200 billion figure); on 2026-06-05 the President said an offering was still under consideration but not rushed, and analysts quoted by trade press described the effort as stalled. The administration's stated aim of keeping government guarantees (May 2025) differs from the chapter's goal of a market without explicit or implicit guarantees, and a House member introduced legislation on 2026-06-25 to set rules for release from conservatorship.

timeline.event: President Trump said the government would keep its guarantees and oversight of the companies as an offering was considered (trade-press account of statements on 2025-05-21 and 2025-05-27).

FHFA Director Pulte said Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac would remain in conservatorship while the government explored selling up to 5 percent of their shares, and expected a presidential decision on an offering by early 2026 (per HousingWire).

Fannie Mae's Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-03-31 states that FHFA raised its agency mortgage-backed securities investment limit in January 2026 (month only; the first of the month is used), which drove much of a $36.3 billion increase in its retained mortgage portfolio to $168.7 billion against a $225 billion cap in its Treasury senior preferred stock agreement; the filing does not mention a $200 billion directive and does not discuss an exit from conservatorship.

Scotsman Guide reports that the President directed the companies to buy $200 billion of mortgage-backed securities, that Pulte said a decision on an offering would likely come within a month or two, and quotes an attorney saying the purchases would almost certainly delay an offering for the foreseeable future.

HousingWire, citing Bloomberg, reports that the President said an offering was not off the table but not a rush; it notes the last reported discussion of an offering was in November 2025, that both stocks were down more than 30 percent for the year, and that Pulte was to become acting Director of National Intelligence from 2026-06-30.

Rep. Scott Fitzgerald introduced the Sustainable Homeownership Act and two related bills, including statutory guardrails for releasing Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac from conservatorship; referred to committee.

Fannie Mae's second-quarter 2026 results release, filed with the SEC, still describes the company as in conservatorship, says its capital requirement is not currently in effect during conservatorship, reports a senior preferred stock liquidation preference of $234.2 billion at 2026-06-30 and a net worth of $116.5 billion, and says nothing about an exit from conservatorship or a public offering.
